content.query:
union isfuzzy=true
    (datatable(TimeGenerated: datetime, _ResourceId: string, Metric: string, Value: real)[]),
    (Perf
    | where ObjectName in ('Processor', 'Processor Information') and CounterName == '% Processor Time'
        and InstanceName in ('_Total', 'total')
    | project TimeGenerated, _ResourceId, Metric = 'Cpu', Value = CounterValue),
    (Perf
    | where ObjectName == 'Memory' and CounterName in ('% Committed Bytes In Use', '% Used Memory')
    | project TimeGenerated, _ResourceId, Metric = 'Memory', Value = CounterValue),
    (InsightsMetrics
    | where Namespace == 'Processor' and Name == 'UtilizationPercentage'
    | project TimeGenerated, _ResourceId, Metric = 'Cpu', Value = Val),
    (InsightsMetrics
    | where Namespace == 'Memory' and Name == 'AvailableMB'
    | extend Total = todouble(parse_json(Tags)['vm.azm.ms/memorySizeMB'])
    | where Total > 0
    | project TimeGenerated, _ResourceId, Metric = 'Memory', Value = 100.0 * (1 - Val / Total))
| where isnotempty(_ResourceId)
| extend rid = strcat_array(array_slice(split(tolower(_ResourceId), '/'), 0, 8), '/')
| where '*' in ({Workload}) or set_has_element(dynamic([{WorkloadIds}]), rid)
| summarize CpuAvg = round(avgif(Value, Metric == 'Cpu'), 1),
    CpuP95 = round(percentile(iff(Metric == 'Cpu', Value, real(null)), 95), 1),
    MemoryP95 = round(percentile(iff(Metric == 'Memory', Value, real(null)), 95), 1) by id = rid
| extend Fit = case(CpuP95 > 85 or MemoryP95 > 90, 'Under pressure',
    CpuP95 < 20 and (isnull(MemoryP95) or MemoryP95 < 50), 'Possibly oversized', 'Within range')
| project id, Fit, CpuAvg, CpuP95, MemoryP95
| order by case(Fit == 'Within range', 1, 0) asc, CpuP95 desc

content.json: *Possibly oversized* is a 95th percentile CPU under 20% with memory under 50%: check the busiest period of the month before resizing. Memory on Windows is committed bytes in use.

### Assessment
The questions of the Well-Architected checklist for each pillar, for the design, process and testing that no
setting shows. Answer each for the workload being reviewed: **Yes**, **Partly**, **No** or **Not applicable**
(hover over a question's name for the whole question). Each pillar is scored from its answers, and every No or
Partly is listed at the bottom as the gaps to act on. Where this workbook has evidence for a question, the table
says where to look.

The answers are workbook parameters: to keep them, **Save** the workbook once answered (or **Save As** a copy per
workload, and per review date). Export the tables to Excel for the review record.

### Reliability
The [Reliability checklist](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/well-architected/reliability/checklist) explains each question and what good looks like.

parameters.name: RE01
parameters.label: RE:01 Simplicity
parameters.description: Is the design kept as simple as the business requirements allow, with nothing that does not add value?

parameters.name: RE02
parameters.label: RE:02 Critical flows
parameters.description: Have the user and system flows been identified and rated by how critical they are?

parameters.name: RE03
parameters.label: RE:03 Failure modes
parameters.description: Has a failure mode analysis been done for each critical flow and its dependencies?

parameters.name: RE04
parameters.label: RE:04 Targets
parameters.description: Are availability and recovery targets (SLO, RTO, RPO) defined and agreed with the business?

parameters.name: RE05
parameters.label: RE:05 Redundancy
parameters.description: Is there redundancy at every layer, across availability zones and, where the targets need it, regions?

parameters.name: RE06
parameters.label: RE:06 Scaling
parameters.description: Does the workload scale in time to meet demand, automatically where it can?

parameters.name: RE07
parameters.label: RE:07 Self-healing
parameters.description: Do components cope with transient faults and failed dependencies (retries, timeouts, circuit breakers, queues)?

parameters.name: RE08
parameters.label: RE:08 Resilience testing
parameters.description: Is resilience tested, for example with fault injection or Azure Chaos Studio?

parameters.name: RE09
parameters.label: RE:09 Disaster recovery
parameters.description: Is there a documented disaster recovery plan, with restores and failover tested against the targets?

parameters.name: RE10
parameters.label: RE:10 Health model
parameters.description: Is health measured and modelled, with alerts on the signals that show the workload is degraded?

parameters.name: RENotes
parameters.label: Notes
parameters.description: Accepted risks, owners and dates for Reliability, kept with the saved workbook.

content.json: **Notes:** {SENotes}

### Cost Optimization
The [Cost Optimization checklist](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/well-architected/cost-optimization/checklist) explains each question and what good looks like.

parameters.name: CO01
parameters.label: CO:01 Accountability
parameters.description: Does the team know what the workload costs and who is accountable for it?

parameters.name: CO02
parameters.label: CO:02 Cost model
parameters.description: Is there a cost model that estimates cost from expected usage and growth?

parameters.name: CO03
parameters.label: CO:03 Cost data
parameters.description: Is cost data collected, tagged by workload and reviewed regularly?

parameters.name: CO04
parameters.label: CO:04 Guardrails
parameters.description: Are there budgets, alerts and policies that catch unexpected spend?

parameters.name: CO05
parameters.label: CO:05 Best rates
parameters.description: Are the best rates in use: reservations, savings plans, Azure Hybrid Benefit, dev/test pricing?

parameters.name: CO06
parameters.label: CO:06 Billing increments
parameters.description: Is usage aligned to how each service bills (instance sizes, hourly units, tiers)?

parameters.name: CO07
parameters.label: CO:07 Component costs
parameters.description: Are idle or oversized components removed or resized?

parameters.name: CO08
parameters.label: CO:08 Environment costs
parameters.description: Do non-production environments cost less than production (smaller sizes, shut down out of hours)?

parameters.name: CO09
parameters.label: CO:09 Flow costs
parameters.description: Is spending prioritised by the business value of each flow?

parameters.name: CO10
parameters.label: CO:10 Data costs
parameters.description: Are storage tiers, retention and log ingestion matched to how the data is used?

parameters.name: CO11
parameters.label: CO:11 Code costs
parameters.description: Is code efficient in the resources it uses (calls, compute, data transfer)?

parameters.name: CO12
parameters.label: CO:12 Scaling costs
parameters.description: Does capacity scale in as readily as it scales out, so it follows demand?

parameters.name: CO13
parameters.label: CO:13 Personnel time
parameters.description: Is the time people spend running the workload measured and reduced?

parameters.name: CO14
parameters.label: CO:14 Consolidation
parameters.description: Are resources and responsibilities consolidated where that lowers cost without adding risk?

parameters.name: CONotes
parameters.label: Notes
parameters.description: Accepted risks, owners and dates for Cost Optimization, kept with the saved workbook.
